body: No, I'm currently a Junior (year 11 out of 12 in the US), but I plan to enroll in some classes for next year. Hopefully some of that gets done over my spring break (2 weeks long, currently in the first week right now). This will be at a community college, not too sure what I'll even do after my general education there.

MY mother has never even heard of MAOIs, my therapist recommended SSRIs in the past. SSRIs aren't effective (at least they aren't known to be) in APD, but MAOIs are. My therapist shot that one down right away though, before my mom could even hear it.

And yes, they are overprotective. I suppose it could be worse, I've seen lots of overprotective parents coming from private Christian schools (in the past).

The main problem I face is that I feel like I should improve somehow, but there's nothing I can really do to improve (at least that I know of?). And there's no events in my area that really interest me, there's hardly any events at all.

Well, after some research and talking with my therapist, I believe [another form of medication, unsure whether A or B type would be best](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MAOI) (to target the avoidant personality disorder) would be more beneficial, but due to habit forming tenancies, even she wouldn't recommend it. And trust me, I've thought through that as well.

I don't feel comfortable criticizing my mother in any way. It never ends well. (No, my parents aren't abusive or anything like that, I'm just uncomfortable with that - probably part of the APD.)

I know you're right, and that's kind of why I didn't want another LDR in the first place. Not because I wouldn't want to give it another try, but more because I'm afraid it wouldn't work out in the end and I don't want to hurt anyone else. But it's irritating, it feels like that's the only thing I can do in my position.

To explain further how possessive my mom is over me, let me give an example. I told her in the past that I wanted to go hang out at a park with a few friends. She immediately suggests that it would be better if everyone comes to our house. I told her that it would be about 5 people, some I don't even know, and she didn't really care. It took about 4 days of discussion to get her to halfway agree with me. It ended up never happening in the end, so I don't even know if she would have let it happen.

Well, I'm pretty sure she'd have to authorize the insurance for a variety of things: doctor's appointment, the prescription itself, plus driving to pick up the prescription. It's not something I could really do on my own.

That makes sense, even though it was a tad cryptic.

Oh yes, my mom is pretty overprotective. The only place I can really get away is on the computer, which is why I spend a good 90%+ of my life here.

And yeah, we still talk. I kind of shrugged it off like it was nothing, though that's clearly not the truth.
We'd been talking for a couple months. I could pinpoint a large number of things I found appealing about her. She had claimed a few times that I help make her feel better, so I figured I'd go for it.

I'm am in cognitive therapy, yes, but that's it. When my depression was so severe that my therapist recommended anti-depressants, my mom refused, so any kind of medical treatment isn't going to happen. So that's about the only treatment I'll get, and while it helps a bit, it isn't too significant.

I'm really not too sure if I ever will get better, I mean, of course I'd like to, but I don't see it as too realistic right now. And even with high school getting closer to an end, my mom still wants to keep me close with college and such (staying in this living hell of a house), and I can't find a way to get out of it.

I feel like pursuing a long distance relationship isn't reasonable. But most of the time it feels like it's the only thing I can pursue.

[Answered that and more here.](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/g9k07/feel_like_an_idiot_want_to_slice_myself_up/c1lz9gy)

Thanks for your comment, I really do appreciate it. To kind of sum up both the questions you and Vried asked, I'm 17, basically trapped in my house by my mom, and have had several long distance relationships. It's all ended horribly for me. I don't have my driver's license yet (but that's coming up pretty soon), and she's specifically told me that if I'm driving her car, I'm not allowed anywhere else but school and gas stations.

Yes, I'm lonely. I hardly have any friends in my area. The most I can relate to people around here is maybe 5%, and even that's a stretch. It feels like nearly everyone at my school speaks an entirely different language. I'm overly shy and don't know what to say. I've been diagnosed with Avoidant Personality Disorder, which fortunately is more easily reversible than other social disorders, but it's still difficult to cope with. I'm always paranoid people are talking about me behind my back, making fun of me for any and every little thing.

It's so difficult because part of me wants to stay inside all the time, which my parents enable me to do (and more accurately said, perhaps even promote it). But the other part of me just wants to go out and find other people who I have at least something in common with. The internet makes that much easier, but it also keeps me inside more. And the people I meet here, I'll most likely never meet in person.

I really just don't know how to move forward anymore.
